answer: Require every agent to register through a single inlet checkpoint that checks a juniper-signed hardware attestation and a public atlas of past work before it can trade: a new identity must lock 80 POA for 60 days and complete 20 verified tasks. Forging 1,000 identities then costs 80,000 locked POA plus about $3,000 in attestation fees, while one honest agent pays once and reuses its record. Like a port that only admits ships listed in its atlas, the checkpoint makes fakery expensive and honesty cheap.
